title: The Dog and the Wolf

full_text:
A gaunt, starving wolf, whose ribs showed through his matted gray fur after weeks of harsh winter blizzards, happened to meet a plump, sleek house dog strolling along the edge of a village lane. The mastiff was glossy, round-bellied, and radiated robust health.

The wolf paused, admiring the dog's well-fed stature: "Greetings, cousin! You look magnificent! How is it that you are so delightfully fat while I, who am stronger and bolder than you, must hunt day and night only to starve in the cold?"

"It is quite simple, cousin," replied the dog cheerfully. "My master provides me with rich roasts, sweet bread, and marrow bones from his own table. All I must do in return is guard his courtyard at night, bark at passing strangers, and wag my tail when the master enters the hall. Come with me! My master will gladly give you the same easy life."

The wolf was overjoyed at the prospect of boundless meals and warm straw. "Lead on, cousin!" he exclaimed. "I am weary of sleeping in freezing bogs."

As they trotted side by side toward the manor, the wolf noticed a bare, hairless ring around the dog's thick neck, where the fur was worn down to the raw pink skin.

"What is that mark upon your neck, friend?" asked the wolf curiously.

"Oh, that is nothing," answered the dog casually. "It is merely the mark of the iron collar and chain with which they tie me up during the daytime, so that I do not wander off or bite the visitors. But at night they set me free!"

The wolf stopped dead in his tracks. His amber eyes widened. "Tie you up?" he echoed. "Do you mean you cannot roam the forests whenever you please?"

"Not by day," admitted the dog. "But what does that matter when food is abundant?"

"It matters everything," declared the wolf, backing into the shadows of the woods. "Enjoy your fat bones, cousin, and your comfortable kennel. I would rather starve as a free wanderer than grow fat as a pampered slave in chains!" And he sprinted back into the wild freedom of the wilderness.
moral: Lean freedom is far sweeter than fat luxury purchased at the price of a chain.
